name: CA-43
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The D+27 baseline, Waters' incumbency, and a 97% market price all point to a safe Democratic hold; the challenger has no visible fundraising or outside support. No evidence justifies moving from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late scandal or unusually low-turnout top-two general could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Maxine Waters, a longtime incumbent in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by 27 points, advanced to the general election against Republican Cristian Morales. Waters has raised over $860,000 and holds a cash advantage, while Morales shows no reported fundraising or outside support. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. No public general-election polling exists, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. The expected margin is roughly 28 points Democratic, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polls. Barring an extraordinary development, Waters is positioned to win another term comfortably.
